name: android-log-mcp

tools.name: logcat_app_launches
tools.description:
Report recent app launches with computed timings — use this for "how long does cold start take / time to first onResume".
For each launch: cold/warm/hot, the launched activity, and a timeline relative to the launch request: process start (am_proc_start), Activity onCreate, onStart, onResume (from wm_on_*_called events in the app process), Displayed (time to initial display, TTID) and Fully drawn (TTFD, only if the app calls reportFullyDrawn()).
This tool only reads logs; launch the app yourself first (e.g. `adb shell am force-stop <pkg>` then `adb shell am start -W -n <pkg>/<activity>`), or ask the user to tap the icon, then call this.

device.description: adb serial. Omit when only one device has logs.

package.description: Exact application id. Omit for all apps.

from.description: Default: last 30 minutes. Same formats as logcat_search.from.

tools.name: logcat_crashes
tools.description:
List Java crashes, native crashes (tombstones) and ANRs, newest first, already parsed and grouped — use this instead of searching for "FATAL EXCEPTION" yourself.
Sources: crash/system/events log buffers (AndroidRuntime FATAL EXCEPTION, libc "Fatal signal" + DEBUG tombstone lines attributed to the crashed pid, am_anr + "ANR in" block) plus the device DropBox (data_app_crash / data_app_native_crash / data_app_anr), which also covers crashes from before recording started and ANR thread dumps.
Pass `id` (e.g. "cr3") for full detail: complete stack / Caused-by chain, the crashed process's last 40 log lines before the crash, and for ANRs the reason plus main-thread trace (or why traces are unavailable). If only one crash matches, detail is returned automatically.

device.description: adb serial. Omit when only one device has logs.

package.description: Exact application id. Omit for all apps.

from.description: Same formats as logcat_search.from. Default: everything recorded.

id.description: Crash id from a previous list (e.g. cr3, anr1) to get full detail.

tools.name: logcat_search
tools.description:
Search recorded logcat lines (buffers main, system, crash, events) of one device. Returns matching lines oldest→newest in a compact format; by default the NEWEST `limit` matches.
Filtering = `filter` (Android Studio Logcat query syntax) AND the structured params (package, tags, min_level, from, to). All parts are ANDed.
Filter syntax (Android Studio): key:value contains (case-insensitive), key=:value exact, key~:regex (RE2, case-sensitive), -key:value negates. Keys: tag message package process line level age is, plus extensions pid tid buffer (main|system|crash|events). level:error = error and above (also accepts V D I W E F). age:5m. is:crash, is:stacktrace. Bare words search the whole line.
Combining: `&` AND, `|` OR (put spaces around them), parentheses group. Space-separated terms are ANDed, EXCEPT repeated positive terms on the same key, which are ORed: `tag:A tag:B` = A OR B; use `message:foo & message:bar` for AND. Quote values with spaces or colons: message:"Start proc".
Examples:
  tag=:OkHttp tag=:MyRepo level:debug
  is:crash | tag~:"^am_(anr|crash)$"
  message~:"Displayed com\.foo" -tag:chatty
Invalid filters return an error with the position and a fix; nothing is guessed. The response echoes how the filter was interpreted — check it.
The `package` param is an EXACT application id covering all its processes (filter's package: is a substring match).
Paging: response gives `before`/`after` cursors. To wait for new lines (e.g. while the user reproduces), pass `after` plus `wait_ms` (≤25000).
The first call for a device starts recording it and backfills its log buffer (waits up to 10 s); a "backfill in progress" note means results may be incomplete: call again.
Use view="summary" first for broad or unknown time ranges (counts by level/tag/package, top repeated messages).

device.description: adb serial. Omit when only one device has logs.

filter.description: Android Studio Logcat query, e.g. `tag=:OkHttp level:warn -message:heartbeat`. Optional.

package.description: Exact application id; matches lines from ALL its processes (com.foo, com.foo:remote), including processes that have since died.

tags.description: Exact tag names, ORed together, e.g. ["OkHttp","MyRepo"].

from.description: Start time, inclusive. Device-local `2026-10-10 01:20:00` or `01:20:00` (= device's today), ISO-8601 with offset, or relative like `30m`, `2h` (= device now minus that).

to.description: End time, exclusive. Same formats as `from`. Default: now.

limit.description: Max matching lines to return (output is also capped at ~30k chars).

context.description: Also show N lines before/after each match from the same process (like grep -C).

before.description: Cursor: return matches older than this (from a previous response).

after.description: Cursor: return matches newer than this (from a previous response or logcat_status).

wait_ms.description: With `after`: block up to this long until at least one new match arrives.

tools.name: logcat_status
tools.description:
Starts recording the device, or extends it with record_for (max 24h; "0" stops). Then reports adb/device/recording state and a `cursor` marking "now" (pass it as `after` to logcat_search to see only what happens next, e.g. while the user reproduces a bug); call it first if unsure which device is connected.
Recording starts on use: the first log tool call for a device backfills what is still in its log buffer, waiting up to 10 s. If the response says backfill in progress, call logcat_status again before using a cursor (no cursor is returned until the backfill has caught up).
Each device stops recording after a while without log tool calls (shown in the response); record_for keeps it recording until a deadline regardless of calls.
With several connected devices and no `device`, nothing is started: pass device=<id>.
With `package`, also reports install state and live/recently-dead processes (pid, process name, start/end time), including multi-process names like com.foo:remote.

device.description: adb serial or device ID. Omit when only one device is connected.

record_for.description: Keep recording this device for this long, independent of calls: a duration with a unit like 30m, 2h or 1h30m (max 24h; the deadline never shortens). "0" stops recording the device now and removes the pin.

package.description: Exact application id, e.g. com.example.app. Optional.

instructions:
Android logcat recorder. Recording starts on use: the first log tool call for a device starts recording it and backfills what is still in the device's log buffer (the call waits up to 10 s for that). Each device stops recording after a while without calls; stored logs stay queryable across sessions.
Typical flows: crashes/ANRs → logcat_crashes. Startup time → logcat_app_launches. Anything else → logcat_search (use view="summary" first for wide ranges).
To capture a reproduction: logcat_status → take `cursor` → user reproduces → logcat_search(after=cursor, wait_ms=20000). If logcat_status says "backfill in progress", call logcat_status again before using a cursor.
To keep recording without calls (e.g. a long reproduction), call logcat_status(record_for="30m"); record_for="0" stops.
All times are device-local; responses state the device timezone.
